question.problem: Consider a matrix equation $B\,x=A\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\times 2$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$

current_example.problem: Consider a matrix equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d},$ where $A$ and $B$ are $10 \times 10$ non-singular matrices, while $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$ are $10 \times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $\mathbf{x}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse $B^{−1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d}$ by $B^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{10}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
